tyler: FYI I just saw a regression in 95p streamed latency on a small subset after enabling mini-coalesce + aggressive KV warmup. baseline was fine, but streams now show extra 50-120ms tail on ~1% of requests.

maria: which model/config? kernel selection changed too?

tyler: gpt-medium-8k, quantized. We flipped coalesce window down to 6ms and enabled prefetch streaks. kernel affinity bumped to prefer small-kernels for short sequences.

raj: can you paste the perf trace? any partial-decode backpressure events?

tyler: dropping trace snippet: ```
[2026-03-18T14:02:12Z] admit req id=0x9a kernel=small prefetch=1 coalesce_ms=6 tokens=3
[2026-03-18T14:02:12Z] decode start req=0x9a partial=true kv_miss=true
[2026-03-18T14:02:12Z] decode pause preemptive_flush reason=token_budget_exceeded owner=req=0x3c
[2026-03-18T14:02:12Z] resume decode req=0x9a kernel_swap small->large cost=1.9ms
```

ev an: looks like a preemptive flush triggered by token_budget for another request causing kernel swap. kernel swap + KV refill = regret.

maria: is token_budget global or per-queue? our change made it per-queue but admission still uses a global token cap calculation.

tyler: admission uses queue-weighted token targets, but the flush gating used global outstanding token budget to decide preemptive pause. mismatch.

kevin: hypothesis: mini-coalesce increases likelihood of short requests being coalesced with long ones, raising partial-decode churn. If kernel affinity switches on resume, overhead spikes.

raj: two options: (1) make preemptive flush decision use same token-budget view as admission (per-queue weighted), or (2) add a fast-path: if anticipated resume needs same kernel, avoid swap by deferring flush up to X ms.

maria: +1 for per-queue budget alignment. Also add telemetry: tag preemptive-flush events with kernel_affinity_before/after and kv_warm_state.

tyler: quick experiment I ran: aligned budgets -> reduced 95p tail by ~40ms on sampled traffic. but saw more head latency for medium-length requests (+10ms) because we delayed flushes.

kevin: we need an SLO-aware knob: prefer tail reduction for streaming endpoints, allow slightly higher head latency. maybe per-route policy.

infra-bot: deploy-preview: mini-coalesce-budgets-aligned rollup -> staged to canary (10%); rollout ETA 15m.

evan: also saw KV eviction churn in the same window. when kernel swapped, KV keys got reloaded causing extra GPU memcpy. we should consider KV prefetch hints on resume.

tyler: agreed. plan: 1) align budget views 2) add resume-hint to request context so KV loader can prefetch predicted keys 3) add metric kv_prefetch_hit_rate and kernel_swap_latency breakdown.

raj: small config patch I can push today. will instrument metrics and run canary. if we still see regressions, we'll try the deferred-swap fast-path.

maria: thanks. can you post the canary link + short query to reproduce on sandbox? I can run an angled workload with mixed short/long streaming sequences.

tyler: posting repro in #eng-dex and attaching a short script. TL;DR: mix 70% short (3-6 tokens), 30% long (>40 tokens), enable mini-coalesce, kernel affinity=auto.

kevin: one more thought: the scheduler could add a tiny jitter on early-send for coalesced groups to reduce alignment with global flush windows (smear effect). that might reduce simultaneous kernel swaps.

raj: good idea. add jitter up to 2ms per request, configurable. will bench.

tyler: thanks all. I'll follow up with metrics after canary finishes (~30m).

infra-bot: canary metrics: 10% traffic, 30m window -> 95p streamed latency delta = -38ms, head median +8ms, kv_prefetch_hit_rate +12%.
